summary: Two parts that sit side by side when the window is wide and stack when it is not, and that drop by priority when it is short: one flow, so each part is written once and not copied per layout. Decided by window size and never by content.

side.doc: 0/1 expression: 1 side by side, 0 stacked. Default: the width reaches sideAt

sideAt.doc: Width in dp from which the parts sit side by side, when side is not given

width.doc: The width the split has. Give it when the split is not the whole window (the window minus your padding)

ratio.doc: The first part's share of the width when side by side

firstHeight.doc: The first part's height when stacked, spacing included; the second gets the rest. 0: half the height

gap.doc: Space between the parts when side by side

dropFirst.doc: 0/1 expression: while 1 the first part is gone and the second takes everything

dropSecond.doc: 0/1 expression: while 1 the second part is gone and the first takes everything

first.doc: The first part, on the left or on top. It gets an exact box: fill it

second.doc: The second part, on the right or below. It gets an exact box

pitfalls: Each slot gets a box of exact width and height, so what is inside must fill or be smaller; give firstHeight for a part that needs a fixed height when stacked

A slot cannot read the split's values: the format has no way for a component to hand a computed value to its slot content. When content must follow the layout (a row count, a hidden caption), compute the same 0/1 flag in your document or a local, pass it as side, and read it in the slot
width and height default to the whole window. Inside padding, pass the window minus the padding: flow wraps as soon as the two widths exceed the real space
Weights do not reach through the flow: a part that grows must take the exact box (fillMaxSize)
